title: ר' יוסי בר חנינא

paragraphs: (1) He is a judge and descends into the depth of judgment: Bava Kamma 39a. The unqualified ‘they laughed at it in the West’ refers to Rabbi Yose bar Chanina: Sanhedrin 17b. Tosafot asks: but Nazir, Sheloshah Minim, 42a, presents Rav Acha son of Rav Ika’s statement, then Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s objection, and so forth; ‘they laughed at it in the West’ means they laughed at Rabbi Yose bar Chanina. Tosafot, Nazir, writes likewise. Orach Mishor there in Nazir writes: this requires examination; Tosafot, 29a, write that there were two men named Rabbi Yose bar Chanina. The same question applies to Sanhedrin’s Gemara, which asks: ‘But they sent from there, according to Rabbi Yose bar Chanina,’ and so forth—there were two! End quotation. That is, Sanhedrin’s identification of ‘they laughed’ with Rabbi Yose bar Chanina means Rabbi Yochanan’s student, while the one they laughed at was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher. One cannot say the reverse, that Sanhedrin means Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher, because Sanhedrin mentions Rabbi Yose bar Chanina after Rav Huna. Since Rabbi Yochanan lived very long and died during Rav Huna’s lifetime, how could his teacher be mentioned after Rav Huna? Thus according to that view Nazir necessarily concerns Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher. But this too is impossible: in Nazir they laughed because Rabbi Yose bar Chanina objected to Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, who was the son of Rav Acha bar Yaakov’s sister. Rav Acha bar Yaakov was Rav Huna’s student. If Rabbi Yochanan, who lived long, died before Rav Huna, how could Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher object to Rav Acha son of Rav Ika? Tosafot’s question therefore stands: Sanhedrin and Nazir both concern Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, Rabbi Yochanan’s student. Why does Sanhedrin say that ‘they laughed at it’ is Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, while in Nazir they laughed at Rabbi Yose bar Chanina? Eruvin 48a, beginning: Rabbi Chiyya taught, and so forth; Rabbi Yose bar Chanina laughed at it. Yevamot 88a, end: Rav said, and so forth; they laughed at it in the West. Rabbi Assi said: ‘I heard this matter from a great man’—Rabbi Yose bar Chanina: Bava Kamma 42b. Shabbat 62b: Rabbi Yose B.R. said—in Ein Yaakov, be-Rabbi Chanina—and so forth; Rabbi Abbahu ridiculed it. Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, Rabbi Oshaya’s brother’s son, said—see above, Chananyah, Rabbi Oshaya’s brother’s son—‘I remember standing before my uncle Rabbi Oshaya’s shop when Rabbi Abba bar Zavda passed’ (Yalkut Esther, section 1059, and Yalkut Yehoshua, section 12). Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yose bar Chanina: one of this pair and one of that pair, Berakhot 22b. Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, one says this: Eruvin 103a. Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said: ‘At Usha they instituted,’ Ketubbot 50a. Taanit 13a: Rabbi Abba HaKohen said in Rabbi Yose HaKohen’s name: an incident in which Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s sons died, and he bathed in cold water all seven days. This requires examination, for Yose HaKohen was very early, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s student. See Rabbi Abba HaKohen and you will see there were two, one Rabbi Yochanan’s student. Sanhedrin 30b: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim was eager to ordain Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, but the matter did not succeed. One day he sat before Rabbi Yochanan, who asked: ‘Is there someone who knows that the law follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah?’ Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim replied: ‘This one knows,’ meaning Rabbi Yose bar Chanina. He said: ‘Let him say it.’ He replied: ‘Let the master ordain him first.’ He ordained him and said: ‘My son, tell me how you heard.’ He replied: ‘Thus I heard.’ Meilah 16b: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina taught before Rabbi Yochanan, and so forth; Rabbi Yochanan praised him. Yevamot 27b: he objected to Rabbi Yochanan. HaMaksheh 73a, end: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said, ‘What is Rabbi Yochanan’s reason?’ He sits in the heavenly academy beside Rabbi Yochanan; see Rabbi Chiyya. All this appears to show that Rabbi Yose bar Chanina was Rabbi Yochanan’s student. Berakhot 10b: Rabbi Yitzchak said: Rabbi Yochanan said: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said in Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov’s name. The same chain occurs again there; Rabbi Yose bar Chanina also speaks in Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov’s name on several matters. Sukkah 40b: what does Rabbi Yochanan do with ‘When you sell’? He needs it for Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s teaching. Shabbat 59a, beginning; Ketubbot 78b, end; Sotah 21b: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says this, Rabbi Yochanan says this. Zevachim 14a and 18b. At the end of Berakhot, Mi SheMetu: Rav Yosef bar Chanina; perhaps it should read Yose; see there.

(2) Rabbi Yose bar Chanina and Rabbi Yochanan: the law follows Rabbi Yochanan, Rosh, end of Bava Kamma, chapter 4. Responsa Chavvot Yair asks, question 94: but in HaKotev he wrote the reverse. End quotation. I shall copy the Gemara’s and Rosh’s wording. Shor SheNagach 39a: ‘From whose best property?’ Rabbi Yochanan says from the orphans’ best property; Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says from the guardians’ best property. So too the Jerusalem Talmud there, halakhah 5. Rosh, at the end of that chapter: ‘It seems to me the law follows Rabbi Yochanan, who was Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s teacher, as evident in HaGozel Batra 112b: Rabbi Yochanan wondered at it—does one receive testimony when the litigant is absent? Rabbi Yose bar Chanina accepted it from him,’ and so forth. ‘The law does not follow a student against his teacher.’ End quotation. Ketubbot 84a: ‘They shall be given to the weakest among them.’ Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says the weakest in proof; Rabbi Yochanan says for a woman’s marriage settlement. So too the Jerusalem Talmud. Rosh there, section 2: ‘We act according to Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, for he is older than Rabbi Yochanan.’ End quotation. Rosh’s words thus contradict each other. But this is understood by noting why Bava Kamma places Rabbi Yochanan’s words before Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s, while Ketubbot places Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s before Rabbi Yochanan’s. Tosafot, Nazir 29a, says: ‘Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Chanina in our passage must have been a tanna, and is not the amora mentioned in the Talmud: Resh Lakish speaks in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name, yet Rabbi Yose bar Chanina was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, whom Rabbi Yochanan ordained in Sanhedrin, as above. How could Resh Lakish speak in his name? Surely there were two.’ End quotation. Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah 1:1 and Kilayim 4:4: Resh Lakish said in Rabbi Yehudah be-Rabbi Chanina’s name. In that matter it is a scribal error and should read Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, as in other texts of Nazir: Resh Lakish said: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said, against our reading Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said: Resh Lakish said. Thus Rosh’s words are clear and sound, founded upon fine-gold bases. Bava Kamma places Rabbi Yochanan first because Rabbi Yose bar Chanina was his student; Rosh therefore rules according to Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher. Ketubbot places Rabbi Yose bar Chanina first because that man was a tanna, Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher; Rosh therefore follows Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, who was older. This is true and correct. The surprise grows: how did he forget his own statement in Responsa Chut HaShani, from Tosafot in Nazir above, that there were two men named Rabbi Yose bar Chanina? This also justifies the several cases in which Rabbi Yochanan speaks in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name, and Rabbi Yose bar Chanina is put before Rabbi Yochanan. In HaKones he is put even before Rabbi Yochanan’s teachers: how do we appraise? Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says a seah within sixty seahs; Chizkiyah says a stalk within sixty stalks; Rabbi Yannai says a tarkav within sixty tarkavs. Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yannai were Rabbi Yochanan’s teachers; see their entries. How could the arranger place a student before his teacher’s teachers? Rather, Tosafot’s explanation is true: there were two, one older than Rabbi Yochanan. It also justifies Tosafot and the Jerusalem Talmud cited above, where Resh Lakish spoke in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name. HaMegareish 86b: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said: Resh Lakish said. Jerusalem Talmud, Yom HaKippurim: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina said: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said. Tefillat HaShachar 26b and Shekalim, chapter 4: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says this, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says this. He places Rabbi Yose bar Chanina before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher; rather, this Rabbi Yose bar Chanina is older than Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and Rabbi Yochanan. Shabbat 147b: Rabbi Chama—in Rosh, Rabbi Yose—be-Rabbi Chanina says this; Rabbi Yochanan says this. Rosh rules according to Rabbi Yochanan. Thus Rabbi Yose bar Chanina must be a scribal error, since, if his words were placed before Rabbi Yochanan’s, he should have ruled according to Rabbi Yose bar Chanina. Understand this. At the end of Tosefta, Arakhin, Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says: ‘Come and see how harsh is the dust of the seventh year.’ It appears this Rabbi Yose bar Chanina was early, since he was included in the Tosefta. Sifrei, beginning of Devarim: Rabbi Benaah says this; Rabbi Yose bar Chanina says this—see there for several things. Rabbi Benaah was Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher; see his entry. This is clear proof that there were two Rabbi Yose bar Chaninas. Since there were two, examine which is the first and which the second.

(3) Rabbi Abbahu transmitted in his name and ridiculed his words; see above. Rabbi Avin said in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name. He objected to Rav Acha son of Rav Ika; see above. Rabbi Assi transmitted in his name; see above. Rabbi Bisna; Guryon. He spoke in Rabbi Huna’s name: Berakhot 52b. It requires examination how he could speak in Rabbi Huna’s name; examine and you will find. I labored and found that he spoke in Rabbi Huna’s name, for Rif and Rosh there read ‘Rabbi Yitzchak bar Chanina said: Rabbi Huna said.’ This pleased me. Examine there, for he often spoke in Rabbi Huna’s name. Rabbi Hila; Rabbi Zeaira bar Chama. Rabbi Zerikan transmitted in his name. Rabbi Chizkiyah; Rabbi Chiyya be-Rabbi Bun; Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda; Chilfaya; Rabbi Chelbo. Rabbi Chama bar Ukva transmitted in his name. In Rabbi Chama, Rabbi Oshaya’s father’s name. In Rabbi Chananyah ben Gamliel’s name. Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi transmitted in his name: Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of HaGozel Kamma. Rabbi Yudan, his sister’s son. Rabbi Yochanan, his sister’s son; this requires examination, see his entry. In Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name. Rabbi Yonah transmitted in his name. Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Bun. He was angry with Rabbi Yose Gelilaya. Rabbi Yose Gelilaya transmitted in his name. In Rabbi Yose bar Chaggaya’s name. Rabbi Yose HaKohen transmitted in his name; see above. Rabbi Yose ben Pazi transmitted in his name; see above. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha transmitted in his name. Rabbi Yasa; Rabbi Levi bar Chayata. In Menachem Yotfai’s name. Rabbi Mani be-Rabbi Yonah. Rabbi Nasa transmitted in his name. Suga was his attendant [Puga in the checked Bavli]. Rabbi Avira. Mar Ukva bar Chama said in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name. Rabbi Krispa transmitted in his name. Ravin sent in his name. Keritot 25b: ‘When Ravin came: Rabbi Yose said: Resh Lakish said.’ It seems to me it should read Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, since we find him speaking in Resh Lakish’s name; see above. Rabbi Tanchum bar Ilai transmitted in his name. The rabbis of Caesarea transmitted in his name: Jerusalem Talmud, Bammeh Madlikin, halakhah 5.
